newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT -- Dlr in for some more sideways trading.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -- Dlr in for some more sideways trading.

text.p: With U.S. financial markets cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve's March 25 policy meeting, the dollar is likely to trade sideways in the near term, technical analysts said on Wednesday.
"Dollar/mark still has a pretty bearish pattern," said I.D.E.A. analyst Ben Morden who noted the dollar stopped at 1.6850-mark near-term resistance on Wednesday.

Morden said the charts indicate the dollar should enjoy good support at 1.6675 marks. However, the I.D.E.A. analyst noted the downside for the dollar may not be so low because "you would find some strong buying if we go below 1.67."
In late trading, the dollar was quoted at 1.6825/30 marks versus 1.6735/40 at the close on Tuesday, and at 122.74/79 yen vs 122.42/47.
"We've got a topping pattern on dollar/mark which suggests we'll go lower. However, we should find some strong buying interest two pfennigs from here," Morden also said.

"Basically, you have sideways trading for dollar/mark versus dollar/yen that is firmer," added Morden who did not rule out further upside for dollar/yen, possibly all the way to 124.10, unless key support at 121.70 is lost.
Again, mark/yen may decide the dollar/yen outlook.
Mark/yen is again facing a test of 73.30, a level that, if taken out, would confirm further mark strength and fresh yen weakness.
Analysts said that scenario cannot be ruled out since the yen is expected to lose some support as the end of Japan's fiscal year nears and yen repatriation dries out.
Turning to dollar/Swiss, Morden said "the risk is that cross would go lower, below 1.44 or 1.4375 Swiss francs."
"Until we go to 1.4250, dollar/Swiss looks weak, and only then does it become very attractive," added the I.D.E.A. analyst who pointed out mark/Swiss could be key.
"Dollar/Swiss may be the negative factor for dollar/mark," Morden added.
Analysts said dollar/Swiss was expected to hold above 1.4310, a strong support level, while 1.4480 offered a tough resistance.
Dollar/Swiss was quoted in late trade at 1.4425/30 versus a close on Tuesday at 1.4385/95.
